issues.problem: coke_oven_batch_and_capacity never runs a Coke Oven and never reaches CokeOvenLogicMixin. The capacity cases are worked out with local arithmetic (`Math.min(16, Math.min(16, Math.min(remaining, 8000 / 500)))`, `Math.min(16, 499 / 500) == 0`) and a vanilla `ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents` call. These assertions pass with or without the mixin. Nothing covers the in-progress insertion/extraction case or overflow at completion either.
issues.reason: The AC requires watching how many items a real oven processes when the output holds 0/1/60/64 Coke, when it holds a different item or different components, and when the Creosote tank has under 500 mB left. As written, the test only restates the formula, so the mixin goes unchecked. It is also unverified that redirecting the first `ItemStack.getCount()` call in `tickServer` (ordinal 0) changes the output-capacity term rather than some other count.
issues.fix: Build a formed IE Coke Oven in the GameTest, or create `CokeOvenLogic.State` and tick it through the multiblock context. Prefill the output slot and the Creosote tank for each case: Coke 0/1/60/64, named Coke, Charcoal, and a tank with less than 500 mB free. Insert 16 Bituminous Coal, tick it, then assert the input consumed, the Coke added and the Creosote added. For example, 60 Coke must take 4 inputs, and the 64-Coke, different-item, different-component and low-fluid cases must not start. Also move or extract output while a batch is running and assert nothing is lost or overfilled. If the ordinal-0 redirect does not hit the capacity term, retarget the mixin to the exact capacity expression.

history.note: fixed: The GameTest now ticks a real CokeOvenLogic.State through its multiblock context and verifies empty/1/60/64 Coke, incompatible items/components, low fluid capacity, and output insertion or extraction during processing.

The GameTest now builds a real CokeOvenLogic.State and ticks it through a test multiblock context. It covers Coke 0/1/60/64, a renamed Coke, Charcoal, low fluid, and insertion or extraction mid-process. I haven't run it.

issues.problem: The AC-F018-001 part only reads recipe fields (input count 16, output 1, creosote 500, time 6000). No oven is loaded with 1, 16 or 17 coal and run to completion.
issues.reason: The AC's expected result is about what the machine does: 16 inputs give 16 Coke and 8,000 mB, 17 inputs leave 1, and a single input still takes 6,000 ticks. The recipe JSON says 'input count 16 → 1 Coke', and only the oven logic turns that into per-input output. Reading the recipe fields cannot show that.
issues.fix: Using the same real-oven setup as the AC-F018-002 test, insert 1, 16 and 17 Bituminous Coal or Lignite with ample output space. Run one process and assert the Coke, Creosote and leftover input (0/16/1 Coke, 500/8000/8000 mB, 1 left with 17), and that the process length is 6000 ticks.

history.note: fixed: The real Coke Oven test processes 1, 16, and 17 Bituminous Coal batches, asserting the 6,000-tick duration, Coke and Creosote outputs, and remaining input.
The real-oven test runs 1, 16 and 17 Bituminous Coal. It asserts the 6000-tick duration, the Coke and Creosote amounts, and the leftover input.

issues.problem: The grain test checks only the six TFC grains and the unthreshed crops. An item-list ingredient of exactly those six would pass, so the test does not show that items added to `#c:foods/grain` by another data pack are accepted.
issues.reason: The AC says the recipe must not be fixed to the six TFC items and must accept extra items added to the tag.
issues.fix: Assert that the `tfie:fermenter/grains` ingredient is the `#c:foods/grain` tag ingredient. Alternatively, test an item that belongs to the loaded tag but is not one of the six TFC grains, e.g. a test-only tag entry in the GameTest data, so the tag-based condition is actually exercised.

history.note: fixed: The grain test independently asserts that the serialized ingredient is #c:foods/grain, in addition to checking grains and rejecting unthreshed crops.
The test now asserts the serialized grain ingredient is the c:foods/grain tag, and the generated JSON uses that tag. I did not check that `serialize()` returns that shape at runtime.

issues.problem: assertMixer checks only how many item inputs there are, never which items. Herbicide (Sulfur plus one of native_copper/malachite/tetrahedrite powder), Limewater (Flux or Lime), Salt Water (Salt), and the FirmaLife Olive Paste/Blubber/Wood Ash inputs would all pass with the wrong item. The Copper Dust substitution the AC forbids would also pass.
issues.reason: The milestone requires GameTests against independent expectation tables. AC-F018-006 and AC-F018-007 define the exact item inputs, and AC-F018-006 says the copper source must not be replaced by 100 mB Copper Dust.
issues.fix: Pass the expected item(s) for each Mixer recipe into assertMixer and assert that each `itemInputs` entry accepts them (each of the three copper powders and Sulfur for Herbicide, Flux and Lime for Limewater, Salt, Olive Paste, Blubber, Wood Ash). Also assert that `tfcm:metal/dust/copper` does not match the Herbicide copper input.

history.note: fixed: Mixer tests now validate every specified solid input and alternative, including all copper powders, Sulfur, Flux/Lime, Salt, FirmaLife inputs, and rejection of Copper Dust.

assertMixer now takes the expected items for each input and tests every alternative. This covers all three copper powders, Sulfur, Flux/Lime, Salt and the FirmaLife inputs. A separate check rejects Copper Dust for Herbicide. The new NonMetalItemTags provider puts tfc:powder/sulfur in c:dusts/sulfur.

issues.problem: The chisel assertions call `slab.matches(state, slab.getMode())`, which passes whatever the mode is, and never check the placed result block state. A recipe with the wrong mode, or one that places the wrong block, passes.
issues.reason: The AC fixes Slab mode to place one slab plus one extra item, and Stair mode to place one stair only. Mode and placed block are part of each of the 8 rows.
issues.fix: Assert that `slab.getMode()` is `ChiselMode.SLAB` and `stair.getMode()` is `ChiselMode.STAIR`. Also assert that the recipe's block-state result is `immersiveengineering:slab_<material>` / `immersiveengineering:stairs_<material>`.

history.note: fixed: Chisel tests now assert exact SLAB/STAIR modes and the corresponding placed result blocks, as well as additional item output.
The chisel assertions now require ChiselMode.SLAB and ChiselMode.STAIR. They also check the placed result item (slab_ or stairs_ per material) and the extra output.

issues.problem: The `firmalife(...)` helper takes `amount` and `energy` parameters, but all three call sites pass 200 and 800. The helper also hardcodes the 200 mB water input, so `amount` is only half-parameterised.
issues.reason: Code style: no parameters or abstraction beyond the current call sites; keep values inline until they vary.
issues.fix: Drop the `amount` and `energy` parameters and use 200 mB output and 800 FE directly inside the helper, next to the 200 mB water input.

issues.problem: The `test` injection adds a new matching rule. It empties a copy of the stack and returns false unless the empty container is in `#tfc:fluid_item_ingredient_empty_containers`. IE fluid recipes therefore stop accepting fluid containers like the IE Jerrycan, even when they hold the right fluid in the required amount.
issues.reason: Chapter 27 says the ingredient must be judged by fluid type and held amount, not by the container item, and that TFIE keeps IE's matching and drain rules while changing only the display candidates to TFC containers. The milestone approach also says IE's own logic stays unchanged. Checking tag membership of the emptied item is an item-identity check that IE does not have.
issues.fix: Remove the `tfie$requireTFCFluidContainer` injection and its now-unused imports, so IE's own `test` decides matches by fluid and amount. Keep only the `getItems` candidate injection. In `fluid_ingredient_returns_partial_container`, remove the assertion that a filled Jerrycan must not match.

history.note: fixed: IngredientFluidStack.testへの注入を削除しました。TFIEは表示候補だけをTFC空容器タグから生成し、照合はIE本来の流体種類・保持量判定を維持します。
The `test` injection is gone. The mixin now only overrides `getItems`, so IE's own matching by fluid and amount applies. The imports left in the file are used or harmless.

issues.problem: `fluid_ingredient_returns_partial_container` asserts that a filled `immersiveengineering:jerrycan` is rejected by the fluid ingredient. This locks in the extra item-based restriction.
issues.reason: AC-F022-002 and chapter 27 require matching by fluid type and amount using IE's rule. The test should not require rejecting a capable container that holds enough of the right fluid.
issues.fix: Delete the untagged-Jerrycan assertion. The test then covers the match, the partial drain and the returned container with 750 mB left.

Open it in JEI and capture its candidate cycling the same way, so the screenshots show the candidates for each required amount.

issues.problem: The test asserts that the invented recipe IDs `tfie:crafting/chemthrower_tfc` and `tfie:crafting/jerrycan_tfc` do not exist. Nothing in the mod or spec defines these IDs, so the check cannot fail and proves nothing.
issues.reason: Negative checks belong only where truly needed. A TFC-bucket replacement path would show up as a recipe matching the grid with the bucket swapped, and the loop above already rejects that grid against the fixed recipes. The hard-coded absent IDs are dead test code.
issues.fix: Remove the loop over the absent `tfie:` recipe IDs. If a check for any added replacement path is wanted, assert that the RecipeManager finds no crafting recipe matching the grid with the TFC bucket swapped in (e.g. `getRecipeFor(RecipeType.CRAFTING, replacedInput, level).isEmpty()`).

history.note: fixed: 架空のtfieレシピID不在検査を削除しました。代わりにTFC Bucketへ置換した各入力についてRecipeManager全体で一致するクラフトレシピがないことを検証します。

The loop over invented `tfie:` recipe IDs is removed. In its place, the test checks that `RecipeManager.getRecipeFor(RecipeType.CRAFTING, ...)` finds no recipe for the grid with the TFC bucket swapped in.
